objects.research_question: Do current PIT states change the conditional probability of a predefined extreme outcome?
assumptions: extreme threshold is preregistered or selected inside training folds only
tail observations are sufficiently numerous for the chosen model
objects.input_contract: PIT return series + approved state variables + event threshold + horizon
objects.output_contract: conditional tail probability distribution, calibration diagnostics, uncertainty interval and unknown state when support is inadequate
objects.reference_implementation: spec-only:R2; deterministic implementation deferred to R4
objects.test_contract: Walk-forward PIT splits; threshold selection inside training only; calibration, PR-AUC, false alarms and lead time reported against all baselines.

objects.research_question: Is the process transitioning into a statistically distinct extreme-risk regime?
assumptions: latent-regime representation is a useful approximation
state count is chosen under complexity control
objects.input_contract: PIT returns, realized volatility and drawdown with training-only model selection
objects.output_contract: regime posterior, transition probability, tail-risk conditional summary and stability diagnostics
objects.reference_implementation: spec-only:R2; deterministic implementation deferred to R4
objects.test_contract: Nested walk-forward model selection; report state stability, held-out calibration, false alarms, transition lead time and complexity penalty.

objects.research_question: Given current price, contract terms and plausible state scenarios, is payoff geometry favorably asymmetric after costs?
assumptions: scenario probabilities are explicitly labeled as assumptions or estimated distributions
transaction costs and premium are included
objects.input_contract: instrument price, contract payoff terms, horizon, implied volatility where relevant, scenario grid/distribution and costs
objects.output_contract: scenario payoff distribution, right-tail capture, left-tail damage, break-even geometry and sensitivity; no trade recommendation
objects.reference_implementation: spec-only:R2; deterministic implementation deferred to R4
objects.test_contract: Replay realized payoffs net of observed costs; verify contractual downside bounds, scenario coverage and sensitivity to IV/transaction-cost assumptions.

objects.research_question: What revenue growth, margin and value-capture path is already embedded in the current enterprise value?
assumptions: discount-rate and terminal assumptions are disclosed
objects.input_contract: PIT enterprise value, revenue, free cash flow, operating margin plus explicit discount/terminal assumptions
objects.output_contract: implied growth/margin/value-capture assumptions, sensitivity surfaces and expectation-gap state; no target price
objects.reference_implementation: spec-only:R2; deterministic implementation deferred to R4
objects.test_contract: PIT reconstruction of implied assumptions; sensitivity grid required; compare held-out expectation revision discrimination versus simple multiple baselines.

objects.research_question: Does a portfolio remain inside declared survival boundaries under adverse distributions and liquidity stress?
assumptions: stress distributions are versioned and disclosed
objects.input_contract: PIT portfolio NAV, returns, exposures, liquid assets, drawdown state, declared ruin/ES/liquidity limits and stress scenarios
objects.output_contract: ruin probability estimate, expected-shortfall distribution, drawdown/liquidity breach frequencies and uncertainty; fail closed on missing portfolio data
objects.reference_implementation: spec-only:R2; deterministic implementation deferred to R4
objects.test_contract: PIT portfolio replays plus synthetic stress; report ruin/breach frequencies, ES, drawdown and liquidity failures versus simpler baselines.

objects.research_question: How should growth-optimal sizing be discounted under estimation uncertainty and explicit survival constraints?
assumptions: payoff/probability estimates are PIT and uncertainty-aware
survival constraints are external hard limits
objects.input_contract: PIT payoff/probability estimates, uncertainty set, portfolio constraints and current wealth/exposure state
objects.output_contract: unconstrained Kelly reference, robust/fractional admissible range, sensitivity to uncertainty and survival constraints; no recommended position size
known_failure_modes: using output as live sizing authority
objects.reference_implementation: spec-only:R2; deterministic implementation deferred to R4
objects.test_contract: Walk-forward repeated-bet simulations with estimation noise and tail stress; compare geometric growth, ruin, drawdown and constraint breaches against baselines.
